## DG6 round 7 (T-DG6-REV-QA-RG-R7): verdict PASS, no new findings

I reviewed candidate `sha256:10f71f24…2e2fc5` (source `d8868b2a5c074b13c04693a88644c25ef2792583`, 2775 files). It recomputes to the same ID at the start and end of my run, over both the working tree and the source commit. The product is byte-identical to `60787d89f` and `3c8b9a3`. Comparing the two manifests shows the only candidate change is the D-240 row of `decisions.md`.

**Open findings** (in `qa-verifier.verifications.json`):
- **F-DG6-911 and F-DG6-951 (Medium): CLOSED_VERIFIED.** The fix `e7cb240e7` is an ancestor of the source commit.
  - `--historical` DG5 to DG1, `--pipeline` and `--register DG6` all exit 0.
  - DG6's 14 history entries are all legal transitions, in time order, and the state matches the last entry.
  - With the fix's FIXING entry removed (stages.json served in memory, repository untouched), the validators fail with exactly "DG6 illegal transition VERIFYING -> REVIEWING" (exit 1). A second mutant, where the state no longer matches the last entry, also fails. The unmodified control passes.
- **F-DG6-990: still closed.** The auditor's round-4 probe finds 0 served DG0–DG7 strings, and the shipped scan passes. Removing migration 0130 makes 4 of the 5 tests fail; dropping only its `kpi.freshness_scan` row makes 3 of 5 fail. Those failures are the intended result.

**Rulings I was asked to judge:**
- **D-240:** I agree. A record fix made after a freeze can only close on a candidate that contains it, so the re-freeze was needed.
- **D-239:** I agree. The five audit-trail reasons cite task and decision ids, not gates, and rewriting the append-only trail would break ADR-0004.
- **F-DG6-952 (Low):** I agree it can be accepted as an observation; only the release auditor can concur.
- **D-229 and D-228 (4):** not defects.
  - My token-sequence probe passes 5/5 through edits, grant changes and concurrent saves.
  - Notification-channel messages carry only a deep link and never a record value.
  - In the cross-organization sweep, 312 operations returned 403 or 404 and changed nothing.

**Suites run on this candidate, all exit 0:**

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Static checks (typecheck, lint, openapi, no-CDN, format, contrast) and both builds | All pass; openapi reports 932 operations |
| Unit, Node 22.22.0 and 24.21.0, both locale settings | 2906 + 2113 + 259 passed in each run (2 skips by design) |
| Integration, twice | 442/442 files, 4370 passed; 122 migrations (0001–0130); 932/932 operations validated; every p6-pending list empty |
| `tests/qa` alone | 437 integration + 61 unit passed |
| Product e2e, both locale settings | 556 passed each (2 demo-only skips, run on the demo stack instead) |
| Root acceptance specs, both locale settings | 288 passed each (18 declared axe skips); 0 axe violations across 108 states per language; loopback-only connections |
| Demo-stack specs | 10/10 in each locale setting |
| Probes: 360/390 px and 200 % text, AUD read-only, XSS, keyboard walkthrough, Arabic export text | All pass |
| A13 kill-and-restart drills | All pass in both integration runs |
| Worker burst | Batched 129.2 jobs/s against 33.6 unbatched; 0 duplicates |

Load figures are provisional (one shared sandbox host): every p95 is under 35 ms with 0 errors. The export check exits 1 only on the dataset gap the register notes already disclose (LOAD-T20 has no second same-scope user).

The installed Node 22 is v22.22.0, not the 22.22.2 the assignment names; I recorded the actual version.

**Interruptions:**
- The 2-hour background-task limit stopped integration run 1 at about 360 of 442 files and the first product e2e run at about 525 of 558 tests, with no failures up to that point. I kept the partial logs and re-ran both suites in full.
- My first load run exited 127 because I wrote the wrong file path in my own script; I fixed it and re-ran.
- Shared disk space briefly dropped to 135 MB while the three reviews ran together. No ENOSPC appears in my logs, and every suite that ran during that window passed.

**Findings: none.** The record is at `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-7/qa-verifier.json`, with evidence under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/round-7/`. The disposable clones were clean before I removed them.
